notes: Maps repository paths to a contribution tier. Read by the contribution marketplace at a pinned commit.
Rule 1: a file matching no glob is treated as forbidden.
Rule 2: a pull request touching several tiers takes the highest one (low < mid < forbidden).
Rule 3: the tier is never inferred from CODEOWNERS. The reverse does hold: every path CODEOWNERS guards is forbidden here, and scripts/check-tiers-codeowners.mjs fails CI when one is not.
Glob dialect: only *, ** and ? (no braces, no character classes, no negation), so every file name is listed as its own pattern.

low and mid are listed file by file: each entry is one file git tracks, never a pattern. A new file therefore lands in forbidden until someone lists it. scripts/check-tiers-codeowners.mjs fails CI on a pattern or an untracked file in either tier.

A file that a forbidden file imports, directly or through other files, is forbidden too: changing it changes the forbidden file's behaviour without touching it. scripts/check-tiers-codeowners.mjs reads the import graph of src/ and extension/ and fails CI when a low or mid file is reached that way.

That rule is why mid is short. Fifteen files listed as mid in the first file-by-file version (four wallet panels, the badges, notices and hints the guarded panels render, the history/price/watch-address helpers, api.ts, wallet.ts, toast.ts) are imported by a guarded screen or by the extension, so they moved to forbidden. Making one of them paid again means first cutting the import, not editing this table. The two files left in mid are imported by nothing outside tests; the gate goes red the day a forbidden file imports one.

The dependency rule looks one way: it forbids what a forbidden file imports, not what imports a forbidden file. A mid file that imports a forbidden one and calls its shared setters at module level could still change how that file behaves once both are loaded together. Neither mid file is loaded by the wallet or the extension today, and src/lib/cardano/gapScan.ts moves to forbidden the day it is wired into the unlock path.

Four more are forbidden for a reason the import graph cannot see on its own: DevWarningBanner.tsx is the web wallet's 'unaudited, do not restore valuable wallets' warning, and src/app/wallet/page.tsx is the only place that renders it, so deleting either line removes a safety warning without touching a guarded file. Once that page is forbidden, Nav.tsx and Footer.tsx, which it imports, follow by the rule above. low is therefore empty; that is the safe direction, not an omission.
Test files are forbidden: deleting the case that pins a check is the cheapest way to disarm the check.
The forbidden list names files that would otherwise fall there by Rule 1 anyway; naming them keeps the decision visible and stops a later mid entry from taking them, since forbidden always wins.
